name: SoK: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Taxonomy, Architectures, Evaluation, and Research Directions

The github.com links appearing in the paper are citations to third-party frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, Smolagents, and AutoGen, not an artifact released by the authors.)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no continuously-updated authors' paper list, leaderboard, or living-survey repository is associated with this work; it is a frozen v1 arXiv PDF/HTML.)
task_domain: Survey / Systematization of Knowledge (SoK). Surveys Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG): RAG pipelines that evolve into autonomous, multi-step, tool-using agentic architectures. Spans knowledge-intensive QA (single-hop, multi-hop, long-form), multi-step reasoning, tool-use/function-calling, web/search-integrated reasoning, decision-making, and memory-augmented long-horizon interaction. It frames the entire class as a sequential decision-making (POMDP) problem rather than a single task domain.
problem_setting: Analytical SoK paper, not a method or system with original experiments. Its core contribution is a unified theoretical framework: it formalizes agentic retrieve-generate loops as finite-horizon Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) with tuple S_ARAG = <S_env, A, Omega, O, pi_theta, M, T>, where the external corpus C is a latent partially observable source, the action space A = A_ret U A_reason U A_tool U {STOP}, and working memory M_t approximates the belief state b_t. It then builds a modular architectural decomposition (Planner, Retrieval Engine, Reasoning Engine/Controller, Memory Systems, Tool Orchestration Layer, Verification/Self-Correction) and a multi-axis taxonomy (architectural/topology, retrieval strategy, reasoning, memory/context). Covers both single- and multi-agent, offline and interactive, supervised and unsupervised settings as surveyed sub-areas. It defines NO controlled experimental protocol, training supervision, or benchmark of its own; it formalizes a budget-constrained objective max_pi E_tau[R_task(y,y*) - lambda * sum_t C(a_t)] but reports no empirical numbers.
what_is_retrieved: N/A as an artifact (the SoK itself retrieves nothing). As surveyed content, Agentic RAG systems retrieve: documents/passages/text chunks (vector/semantic retrieval over external knowledge corpora), tool/API outputs (function-calling observations), web-search results, and agent memory entries (episodic trajectories, reflective feedback, persistent long-horizon memory). Retrieval is modeled formally as a discrete action a_t = Retrieve(q'_t) returning an observation o_t in Omega.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID at the survey level. It explicitly models retrieval against a STATIC/dynamic external corpus C (latent partially observable knowledge source, plus tools/APIs and web search) AND a GROWING agent memory the agent writes (episodic memory, persistent long-horizon memory in vector DBs, e.g., MemoryBank/MemGPT-style). The POMDP treats both external retrieval (observation function O) and memory write/read/prune (belief-state update on M_t) as first-class.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A (survey; defines no retrieval objective of its own beyond a generic top-k retriever in baseline RAG). It instead emphasizes adaptive, state-dependent, iterative retrieval (one-shot vs iterative vs self-refining) controlled by the agent's policy, and surfaces Effective Information Rate (EIR = useful retrieved tokens / total retrieved tokens) and Context Relevance as efficiency-oriented retrieval objectives that penalize context overloading rather than a fixed top-k or completeness target.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the SoK is not a case-based reasoning system and implements no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame Agentic RAG as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It organizes the field around a POMDP formalization, modular architectural components, and taxonomy axes (topology, retrieval strategy, reasoning, memory).
retrieval_unit: N/A (survey defines no single retrieval unit). Surveyed/modeled units: text chunks/passages/documents (the typical observation o_t returned by the retriever), tool-API outputs/observations, web snippets, and memory entries (episodic trajectories, reflective notes, persistent long-horizon memory states). Formally any o_t in the observation space Omega.
index_source: N/A for the SoK (it builds no index). Surveyed Agentic RAG draws on a static/dynamic external corpus C (vector indexes, tools/APIs, live web search) combined with a growing agent memory written online during the control loop (episodic + persistent long-horizon memory persisted into vector databases). The work classifies memory paradigms (dynamic context pruning, episodic memory, persistent long-horizon memory) as the growing/online side.
index_structure_topology: N/A (SoK has no index of its own). It reviews flat vector indexes/databases for documents and for persistent long-horizon memory (MemoryBank, MemGPT), plus graph-structured agentic orchestration substrates (LangGraph graph-structured workloads). Its own organizing structure is a multi-axis taxonomy and a POMDP component map, not an index topology.
retriever_type: N/A (survey; no retriever implemented). Surveyed retrievers are off-the-shelf dense/semantic retrievers and tool/web-search APIs invoked as actions; the LLM acts as the control policy / query constructor (LLM-as-controller) rather than as the retriever. It also notes learned context filters (FILCO, Provence) and self-retrieval/critique (Self-RAG) as variants.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (survey; trains no retriever). It reviews systems where retrieval decisions are driven by the LLM control policy via prompting or fine-tuning (pi_theta), by token/log-probability confidence thresholds (Active RAG/FLARE, contrasted with Agentic RAG), by self-critique (Self-RAG), and by learned/RL or hybrid control policies; as a future direction it proposes RL with stability constraints and Bayesian retrieval-confidence calibration. It standardizes no single learning signal.
query_construction: N/A as a method. Surveyed/modeled: queries are conditionally generated at runtime from the evolving memory state, a_t = Retrieve(q'_t) with q'_t conditioned on M_t (Dynamic Retrieval property). Concrete surveyed constructions include CoT/ReAct thought-conditioned query construction (IRCoT), planner-driven decomposition (Plan-Then-Retrieve, Decomposition-Based Retrieval), and query reformulation/rewriting in self-refining loops. It notes semantic drift as a risk of iterative reformulation.
query_granularity: N/A (survey). Modeled at multiple levels: task-level (one-shot at t=0), and step/state-level (iterative and self-refining retrieval where later retrievals depend on intermediate state M_t). The taxonomy's retrieval-strategy axis (one-shot / iterative / self-refining) is precisely about query granularity over the trajectory.
when_to_retrieve: N/A (survey). Its retrieval-strategy taxonomy spans one-shot (single retrieval then generate), iterative (multiple state-dependent retrievals during one query), and self-refining (retrieval coupled with critique/revision). It explicitly distinguishes Active RAG (token-confidence-triggered, single-pass) from Agentic RAG (policy-driven, multi-step, explicit deliberation).
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (survey defines no single trigger). It catalogs: log-probability thresholds / token heuristics (Active RAG/FLARE, which it explicitly contrasts as NOT agentic), explicit policy-driven reasoning and tool-calling decisions sampled from pi_theta(a_t | M_t) (Agentic RAG), reflection/self-evaluation steps (Reflexion, Self-RAG, RARR), and relevance/critique-driven re-retrieval in self-refining loops. The defining Agentic trait is policy-driven (not confidence-threshold) triggering.
reranking: N/A (survey; no reranking stage of its own). It does not center reranking as a taxonomy axis; instead it foregrounds dynamic context pruning/filtering (FILCO, Provence) and self-refining critique as the post-retrieval selection mechanisms.
retrieved_context_refinement: N/A as a method. Surveyed refinement operations: dynamic context pruning/compression and learned context filtering (FILCO, Provence) to mitigate irrelevant evidence and the lost-in-the-middle effect; self-refining critique/revision of retrieved evidence (Self-RAG, RARR); and memory belief-update operations (selective retrieval augmentation, summarization, pruning of redundant info, learned memory controllers). The SoK frames refinement as belief-state update on M_t.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (the SoK contributes no tool-document-engineering technique). Tool invocation is modeled abstractly as actions in A_tool with outputs returned via the observation function O; it discusses tool reliability evaluation (selection, parameter F1, execution-based sandbox assessment) but not how tool/skill descriptions are indexed.
index_content_separation: N/A (survey; no index-vs-content separation mechanism of its own). It discusses dynamic context pruning (loading/compressing retrieved content before generation) but not a lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure scheme.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A as a contribution. It reviews tool integration via function-calling and agent SDKs/frameworks (OpenAI function calling / Agents SDK, Anthropic tool use, Google ADK, LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Smolagents, AutoGen) and treats tool calling as an explicit multi-step interaction boundary, but it does not center a live-synchronized tool index or a specific protocol such as MCP/RapidAPI as a taxonomy axis.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (survey). It discusses Planner-Executor role separation, multi-agent delegation, and cascading tool-execution errors, but does not center an explicit inter-tool dependency-graph retrieval formalism.
how_retrieved_used: N/A as a method. Modeled formally: retrieved observations o_t are appended to working memory (M_{t+1} = M_t U O(o_t | s_t, a_t)) and the final answer is generated as y = G(M_T) after the policy emits STOP. Surveyed utilization spans prompt/context augmentation, iterative refinement across reflection loops, and feeding validated/refined evidence to a response-synthesis step. Unlike append-only Active RAG, Agentic RAG supports read/write/prune over working memory.
planning_integration: N/A as a method. Planning is a first-class POMDP/architecture element (Planner module governs tool invocation under a control policy). The SoK catalogs design patterns for retrieval-planning integration: Plan-Then-Retrieve, Retrieve-Reflect-Refine, Decomposition-Based Retrieval, Tool-Augmented Retrieval Loop, Multi-Agent Collaboration, Retrieval-Grounded Self-Verification, and Human-As-A-Tool (HITL). Topology axis covers Single-Agent, Planner-Executor, and Multi-Agent RAG. It reviews these rather than committing to one.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: N/A (survey). Its reasoning taxonomy enumerates per-step interleaving styles: Chain-of-Thought, ReAct-style (interleaving reasoning steps with tool actions/observations), reflection-based (per-critique self-evaluation), and tree-based exploration (search over candidate branches with backtracking, e.g., Tree-of-Thoughts). It also contrasts Active RAG per-token interleaving against Agentic RAG per-action/per-tool-call interleaving.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no retrieved-case adaptation mechanism of its own).
retrieved_item_representation: N/A (survey). Surveyed injected forms: raw retrieved passages/text chunks, tool/API outputs, web snippets, and memory representations (episodic trajectories, reflective feedback, summarized contextual knowledge). The SoK abstracts these as structured memory representations M_t approximating the belief state, updated via augmentation/summarization/pruning.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: N/A (survey). Surveyed units span raw passages/documents and tool outputs (low abstraction) up through summarized/consolidated memory and reflective insights (higher abstraction). The SoK does not fix an abstraction level; it treats the unit generically as observations o_t and memory elements.
noise_robustness_mechanism: N/A as a method (the SoK contributes none). It dedicates major analysis to robustness as a needed evaluation dimension: Noise Robustness (extracting answers from distracting context), Negative Rejection (declining when context is absent), and Adaptive Resilience (recovering when the environment changes mid-task), citing RGB/FaithEval/RAGEval. It also diagnoses noise-driven failure modes (retrieval drift, hallucination despite retrieval, compounded hallucination loops) and proposes future counterfactual-retrieval resilience datasets.
memory_type: Survey-level: memory is a central taxonomy axis and architectural module. It distinguishes (1) dynamic context pruning of the active context window (FILCO, Provence), (2) episodic memory (temporally bounded trajectories/feedback, e.g., Reflexion buffer, Generative Agents memory stream), and (3) persistent long-horizon memory across sessions persisted into vector DBs (MemoryBank, MemGPT). Formally, working memory M_t approximates the POMDP belief state b_t. The SoK itself has no memory.
write_back: N/A as a method. Surveyed Agentic RAG systems DO write back: working memory updates each step (M_{t+1} = M_t U {observations/conclusions}), episodic buffers store reflective feedback, and persistent long-horizon memory stores/recalls/updates interaction memories. The SoK frames write-back as belief-state update; it stores nothing itself.
online_growth: N/A as a method. Surveyed memory grows online during the control loop and across sessions (episodic logging per step; persistent memory accumulated across sessions). The SoK itself has no growing store.
write_back_trigger: N/A (survey; no write-back trigger of its own). Modeled/surveyed triggers: per-step belief-state updates after each retrieval/reasoning action; reflective writes after self-critique (Reflexion episodic buffer); and persistent-memory refresh strategies (update/consolidate/decay) for long-horizon memory (MemoryBank/MemGPT). It also flags memory-update timing as a security/robustness concern (poisoning persists across writes).
failure_experience_usage: N/A (survey). It reviews reflection/self-correction patterns that act on poor/failed retrieval or outputs (Reflexion stores reflective feedback in an episodic buffer; Retrieve-Reflect-Refine and Retrieval-Grounded Self-Verification patterns), implying use of failure signals, but it also warns that reflection sharing the generator's parametric biases can reinforce errors (Feedback Reinforcement Instability). It contributes no explicit success-vs-failure storage scheme.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (survey). Surveyed post-write dynamics: belief-update operations (selective augmentation, summarization, pruning of redundant info), persistent-memory refresh strategies that update/consolidate/decay entries over time, and learned memory controllers that retain high-utility signals. It proposes no single canonical post-write policy and flags memory robustness/poisoning as an open problem (10.3).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Survey-level YES (as a framing): the SoK's defining thesis is that Agentic RAG is characterized by a stochastic control policy pi_theta(a_t | M_t) over an action space including retrieval, and it formulates policy optimization as a budget-constrained sequential decision problem (max over pi_theta of E[R_task - lambda*sum C(a_t)]). It surveys policies that are heuristic, hybrid, or learned/RL, and proposes RL with stability constraints as a future direction; it implements no learned policy itself.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Surveyed (not a contribution): Multi-Agent RAG distributes planning/retrieval/generation across agents with shared/aggregated memory (AutoGen multi-agent conversation, CrewAI, LangGraph orchestration, Google ADK). It reviews cross-agent coordination and shared memory, and flags multi-agent retrieval drift via delegation and cross-session leakage as risks; it does not implement cross-agent sharing.
benchmarks: N/A as original experiments (the SoK runs no experiments and reports no results of its own). It catalogs and critiques evaluation frameworks/benchmarks used for (agentic) RAG: RGB (Benchmarking LLMs in RAG), FaithEval, RAGBench (with the TRACe framework: uTilization/Relevance/Adherence/Completeness), RAGEval, CRAG, plus newer rubric-based/contamination-aware frameworks DRACO and CL-Bench. It also references agent-evaluation surveys.
benchmark_family: Survey-level grouping. Primary families discussed are RAG-evaluation / faithfulness-and-noise frameworks (RGB, FaithEval, RAGBench/TRACe, RAGEval, CRAG) and emerging agentic/trajectory-aware evaluation (DRACO, CL-Bench), plus agent-evaluation surveys. It explicitly argues these are mostly QA/multi-hop static, single-forward-pass benchmarks that fail to capture long-horizon trajectory evaluation, dynamic tool invocation, and multi-step interaction; it does not adopt the embodied/web/tool/decision-RL benchmark families as primary axes.
baselines: N/A (survey; no head-to-head method comparison of its own). Its comparative analysis contrasts paradigm classes (static/baseline RAG vs Active RAG vs Agentic RAG) and archetypes (baseline grounded generation, iterative evidence accumulation, reflective refinement, role-separated orchestration, distributed knowledge work, memory-centric long-horizon), anchored by representative systems (RAG, IRCoT, Iter-RetGen, Self-RAG, RARR, Reflexion, HuggingGPT, MRKL, AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, MemoryBank, MemGPT).
key_metrics: N/A as original measurement (no numbers of its own). It proposes/synthesizes agentic evaluation metrics: Progress Rate (PR = successful reasoning steps / total reasoning steps), Effective Information Rate (EIR = useful retrieved tokens / total retrieved tokens), Context Relevance, Faithfulness (TRACe Adherence / NLI), Tool Reliability (parameter F1, execution-based sandbox verification), and robustness metrics (Noise Robustness, Negative Rejection, Adaptive Resilience). It critiques BLEU/ROUGE, Exact Match, Final-Answer Accuracy, Success Rate, and Pass@k as inadequate for agentic systems (Table VII Metric Failure Analysis).
headline_result: N/A (survey; no headline number). Its central contributions are conceptual: (1) the FIRST unified framework modeling agentic retrieve-generate loops as finite-horizon POMDPs S_ARAG = <S_env, A, Omega, O, pi_theta, M, T> with four necessary properties (Iterative Control, Dynamic Retrieval, Tool-Mediated Interaction, State Persistence) plus finite-horizon Termination; (2) a multi-axis taxonomy (topology / retrieval-strategy / reasoning / memory) and modular architectural decomposition; (3) a three-layer evaluation pipeline (component / trajectory / system level); and (4) five doctoral-scale grand research problems (stable adaptive retrieval, formal reasoning evaluation, memory security, cost-aware orchestration, trust calibration). For grounding the diagnosis it cites striking surveyed numbers, e.g., RAG legal tools hallucinating up to 33%, and as few as 5 injected malicious documents causing ~90% attack success.
ablations: N/A (survey; conducts no experiments and reports no component ablations). Its closest analogue is the Cross-Dimensional Trade-Off Analysis (Section IV-E): Retrieval Depth vs Cost, Planning Complexity vs Latency, and Cost/Latency/Token Economics (token amplification scaling with iterative steps), plus the consolidated taxonomy Table III mapping archetypes to topology/retrieval/reasoning/memory/policy and Table IV mapping representative systems to taxonomy dimensions.
evaluation_decoupling: Survey-level YES (as a recommendation, not original measurement). It explicitly argues evaluation must decouple intrinsic/component metrics from end-to-end outcome and proposes a three-layer pipeline: Layer 1 Component-Level (Planner decomposition, Retriever recall/precision, Tool Executor invocation accuracy and parameter F1), Layer 2 Trajectory-Level Coherence (Progress Rate, step-success ratios, memory consistency), Layer 3 System-Level Outcome (final task completion, coordination effectiveness, faithfulness, plus cost/latency/TTFT). It critiques conflating intrinsic retrieval accuracy with final outcome.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Survey-level central thesis: evaluation must assess PROCESS (multi-step reasoning trajectory, tool interaction, decision dependencies), not just final-answer OUTCOME. It introduces trajectory-level metrics (Progress Rate, EIR), an Iterative Reasoning Quality dimension (auditing logical steps, e.g., Reasoning-via-Planning), and warns that final-answer/EM/Success-Rate metrics are 'trajectory blind' and cannot distinguish sound reasoning from lucky guesses. The SoK itself scores nothing.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: N/A as original measurement (no cost numbers of its own). It treats cost as first-class: the POMDP objective subtracts a step-wise cost term lambda*sum_t C(a_t) modeling latency, token consumption, and API limits; Section IV-E analyzes Retrieval Depth vs Cost, Planning Complexity vs Latency, and token amplification (iterative retrieval scaling cost with number of steps); the evaluation pipeline mandates Cost and Latency Awareness (token amplification, Time-To-First-Token); and Grand Problem 10.4 (Cost-Aware Autonomous Orchestration) targets Pareto efficiency (Compute vs Accuracy) and budget-aware multi-agent routing.
context_budget_and_selection_count: N/A (survey; no token budget or k of its own). It frames context budget via the lambda regularizer in the POMDP objective and the Memory/Context paradigms axis: long-context models still need structured context selection (lost-in-the-middle), motivating Dynamic Context Pruning (FILCO, Provence) and budget-aware orchestration. It prescribes no fixed-k or token cap; it advocates adaptive, budget-constrained context construction.
survey_scope_and_axes: Primary organizing axes: (1) a POMDP system-level formalization (S_env, A=A_ret U A_reason U A_tool U {STOP}, Omega, O, pi_theta, M, T) with a property->POMDP-component mapping table and an Active-RAG-vs-Agentic-RAG distinction table; (2) a multi-dimensional taxonomy -- Architectural/Topology (Single-Agent, Planner-Executor, Multi-Agent), Retrieval Strategy (One-Shot, Iterative, Self-Refining), Reasoning (CoT, ReAct-style, Reflection, Tree-based), Memory/Context (dynamic pruning, episodic, persistent long-horizon), and Control Policy (heuristic/hybrid/learned), with cross-dimensional trade-off analysis; (3) core architectural components (Planner, Retrieval Engine, Reasoning Engine/Controller, Memory Systems, Tool Orchestration, Verification/Self-Correction); (4) seven design patterns; (5) a three-layer evaluation pipeline and a metric-failure analysis; (6) industry frameworks and deployment; (7) failure modes/safety (retrieval drift, hallucination despite retrieval, tool misuse/cascading errors, prompt injection, memory poisoning, systemic risk amplification); and (8) five doctoral-scale grand research problems. Coverage window ~2023-2026 (v1 Mar 2026); ~105 references per Semantic Scholar, ~118 numbered HTML bibliography entries.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey/SoK, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset). It reports characteristics of frameworks it catalogs (e.g., RAGBench's TRACe framework with uTilization/Relevance/Adherence/Completeness; RGB/FaithEval for noise robustness and counterfactual adherence; RAGEval/CRAG for keypoint-based factual accuracy and multi-hop coverage) but generates none of its own.
builds_on: Builds on and synthesizes: (1) foundational RAG (Lewis et al. RAG; Gao et al. and the 'RAG meeting LLMs' survey for the static-RAG baseline and survey framing); (2) iterative/active retrieval (IRCoT, Iter-RetGen / iterative retrieval-generation synergy, FLARE/Active RAG); (3) self-refining retrieval and attribution (Self-RAG, RARR); (4) agent reasoning/acting (ReAct, Chain-of-Thought, Plan-and-Solve, Reflexion, Tree-of-Thoughts); (5) modular/neuro-symbolic and controller-executor agents (MRKL, HuggingGPT); (6) context pruning (FILCO, Provence) and lost-in-the-middle analyses; (7) memory systems (Generative Agents, MemoryBank, MemGPT, agentic memory); (8) evaluation frameworks (RGB, FaithEval, RAGBench/TRACe, RAGEval, CRAG, agent-evaluation surveys); and (9) industrial frameworks/SDKs (OpenAI function calling/Agents SDK, Anthropic tool use, Google ADK, LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Smolagents, AutoGen). POMDP/sequential-decision framing draws on the RL/control literature.
contrasts_with: Explicitly positions Agentic RAG against: (1) static/baseline retrieve-then-generate RAG (single forward pass, append-only context, cannot self-correct); and (2) Active RAG (e.g., FLARE) -- it dedicates Table II to distinguishing Active RAG (log-probability/token-heuristic triggers, single-pass forward generation, implicit planning, append-only context, no self-correction) from Agentic RAG (policy-driven reasoning and explicit tool-calling, iterative multi-step planning loops, explicit deliberative phase, read/write/prune working memory, can discard poor retrieval and re-query). As a SoK it also contrasts its formal POMDP-grounded, trajectory-level evaluation stance against prior fragmented, output-only RAG evaluation practice and prior Agentic RAG surveys that lack a sequential-decision formalization.
lineage: Surveys group. A 2026 Systematization-of-Knowledge survey that is distinctive for being the first to formalize agentic retrieve-generate loops as finite-horizon POMDPs and to organize the field around a sequential-decision-making frame (control policy, action space, belief-state memory, budget-constrained objective). It serves as an umbrella/foundational reference connecting iterative/active retrieval (FLARE, IRCoT, Iter-RetGen), self-refining/corrective retrieval (Self-RAG, RARR), agent reasoning (ReAct, Reflexion, ToT), memory systems (MemGPT, MemoryBank, agentic memory), tool orchestration, and agentic evaluation -- relevant to multiple sub-topics in this collection rather than being a method within any single one. It complements the 2025 Singh et al. 'Agentic RAG' survey, adding a formal POMDP backbone, a systemic failure-mode/safety analysis, and a doctoral-scale research roadmap.
